caveat.description: the author's own plain-English limit on the figure, where the research pass gave one - 'Based on respondents' estimates, not records'; 'Size of the pot, not a loss'

confidence.description: the evidence grade, by the published rubric in github.com/demitonapp/disease-economics METHOD.md Section 4: `low` (read second-hand, unverifiable, or a model or estimate), `moderate` (read at source but one organisation's data, people's own estimates, or a sampling problem the caveat names), `high` (read at source and none of those). Carried so the surface can rank its evidence honestly instead of presenting a secondary citation as a measurement

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of a `per_*` figure (AUD, USD, NZD); null for ratios and `none`. The surface prints the amount in this currency, never as a bare dollar sign

denominator.description: what a `ratio_of_other` figure is a share OF: `budget_at_decision`, `budget_at_announcement`, `construction_cost`, `amount_claimed`, `arbitration_cost`, `total_injury_cost` (the vocabulary of github.com/demitonapp/disease-economics schema/finding.schema.json). Null for every other unit

disease_key.description: which of the five margin diseases this finding prices - the SD027 §4.6 disease key (`rework_signal`, `overrun_signal`, `claim_window`, `evidence_gap`, `compliance_gate`)

exposure_basis.description: what the figure is a percentage OF, in words - 'of original contract value'. Stored because the same disease yields 3-5% of one basis and 10% of another, and a bare number without its basis is the most common way a benchmark misleads

exposure_kind.description: who bears the money: `contractor_loss` (the source measured money the contractor loses), `money_at_stake` (it measured how much is in play, not what is lost), `owner_side` (the client pays), or `societal` (workers and the community). Only contractor_loss and money_at_stake may reach the headline ledger

exposure_unit.description: how the figure may be projected: `ratio_of_contract` (multiplies a contract value), `ratio_of_other` (a share of something else, named by `denominator`; never multiplied), `per_wet_day`, `per_incident`, `per_year_industry`, or `none` when no published figure exists. Multiplying a per-day or per-incident figure, or a share of an arbitration bill, by a contract value is nonsense, so the unit is declared rather than assumed

exposure_value.description: the published figure in the source's own unit. A share of contract value is stored as a decimal fraction (10% is 0.10); a per-day or per-incident figure is stored in whole dollars. 0 when the source published no such figure
exposure_value.x-demiton-unit: decimal fraction for ratio_of_contract; AUD for per_wet_day and per_incident

industries.description: ISIC Rev.4 divisions the evidence covers (`F42` civil engineering, `F` construction, `ALL`, `unknown`); the union of the finding's sources. Carried for display and future matching; not yet part of the rule

jurisdictions.description: Where the evidence is from: ISO 3166 codes (`AU`, `AU-QLD`), `GLOBAL` (no limit claimed) or `unknown`; the union of the finding's sources. The exposure service applies a figure to a project only when this holds the project's place, its country, or GLOBAL

label.description: how the finding is named on the surface, in the source's own terms - 'Mean total rework cost (115 Australian civil projects)'

metric_key.description: the finding's stable identifier within its disease, e.g. `rework_total_civil_survey`. The seed's idempotency partner: re-running the seed updates the same row, and a genuinely new finding gets a new key

price_year.description: the year a `per_*` amount is priced in; null otherwise

sample_note.description: sample size, geography, sector and method - what bounds the figure. Null where the source did not disclose it

source_location.description: where in the document to look - 'abstract', 'p.5', 'table 23'. Null when the source did not permit it

source_org.description: the publishing organisation or author of record

source_secondary.description: true when the figure was read only through someone else's citation rather than at the primary document

source_title.description: the paper, report or dataset title

source_url.description: a resolvable link to the source

source_year.description: the year of the source, for a vintage check - a 2001 benchmark and a 2025 one are not the same evidence
